commits.message:
feat(misc#377): put the dev internal ALB listener on the FIPS post-quantum TLS policy (#616)

Part of CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#377 (dev only; the impl and prod PR
closes it)

### What and why

This moves the internal ALB's HTTPS listener in dev to
`ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-Res-FIPS-PQ-2025-09`, the FIPS policy
Elizabeth chose. AWS ties the ALB's backend policy to the listener
policy, so with a FIPS post-quantum listener the ALB connects to the API
targets with `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-0-FIPS-PQ-2025-09`, which offers
hybrid ML-KEM. That is what makes the ALB to API hop hybrid.

The policy is now a variable, `alb_ssl_policy`, whose default is the
current `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06`. Only `dev.tfvars` sets
the new policy, so impl and prod plan no change. A merge to main deploys
dev and prod in the same run, and this keeps prod out of it until dev
has been checked. A follow-up PR sets impl and prod.

### What I checked before the change

- **CloudFront to ALB.** A week of dev connection logs (2026-10-08 to
2026-10-14, 706 connections) shows CloudFront on TLS 1.3 with
`TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` and secp256r1. The new listener policy supports
all of it.
- **ALB to Okta and Entra.** The backend policy also covers the ALB's
OIDC calls. Okta (dev and prod) negotiates TLS 1.2 with
`ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256` on P-256, and Entra negotiates TLS 1.3
with `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`. Both are in the backend policy.
- **Baseline.** The API's handshake log from
[ztmf!613](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/613) recorded 60
`hop=alb` handshakes in dev on 2026-10-14, all TLS 1.3 on X25519.

### Open question the dev rollout answers

AWS lists SecP256r1MLKEM768, SecP384r1MLKEM1024, and X25519MLKEM768 for
its post-quantum policies but does not publish the groups per policy.
Since [ztmf!619](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/619) the
API builds with Go 1.27.3, which supports both X25519MLKEM768 and
SecP256r1MLKEM768, and the API server does not set `CurvePreferences`,
so it takes Go's defaults. If `hop=alb` still logs a classical group
after the dev deploy, the FIPS backend policy does not offer a hybrid
group Go supports, and that question goes to AWS.

### Testing

`terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` pass. `make test-unit`
passes; no Go code changed. After the dev deploy I will check the
`hop=alb` group in the API logs, CloudFront origin errors, and a login
through Okta and Entra.
commits.author: cameron testerman

commits.message:
fix(misc#433): score pillars with the HHS x1.25 formula (#621)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#433. Closes
CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#383.

Pillar scores now use the HHS scorecard formula: the average of the 1-4
answers times 1.25 (sum x 5 / max), instead of adding 1 to each answer
and averaging. The HHS FY25 numbers on record were scored this way, and
checking the FY25 HHS sheet confirms it: every pillar matches sum x 5 /
max, and the overall is the average of the six pillars, which we already
do.

| Answers in a pillar | Before (+1) | After (x1.25) |
|---|---|---|
| all 1 | 2.00 | 1.25 |
| all 2 | 3.00 | 2.50 |
| all 3 | 4.00 | 3.75 |
| all 4 | 5.00 | 5.00 |

An unanswered question counts as a 1, so a pillar with nothing answered
scores 1.25. Blanks only exist on incomplete systems; once a question is
saved one of the four options is always selected. Tier cutoffs and the
system score (average of pillars) are unchanged.

A pillar with nothing answered is still labeled Not Assessed, not
Traditional, and so is a system with nothing answered in any pillar. Its
score stays 1.25 and still counts in averages. The query now returns an
answered count per pillar and per system, and the rollup uses Not
Assessed when it is zero; otherwise the tier comes from the score as
before. A pillar answered all 1s also scores 1.25 but reads Traditional,
because it was assessed.

The change is one expression in the `pillar_scores` CTE in
`backend/internal/model/scores.go`. Scores are computed on read, so
every data call is rescored, which is intended: rescored FY25 then lines
up with the HHS FY25 figures for all but a handful of systems.

## Rider: export labels its score column

The data call export's column I is now headed "Answer Score (1-4)", and
a second sheet, "How scores work", states how the dashboard builds
pillar and system scores from it and why averaging column I directly
will not match. This is the #383 ask; layout and values are otherwise
unchanged.

## Testing

- New `TestPillarScoreHHSFormulaIntegration` recomputes every pillar and
system score in the seed from the raw answers. The seed has one question
per pillar, so the test adds a second, unanswered question to an
answered pillar to cover the partial case, and removes it on cleanup.
Checked that it fails with blanks counted as 0 and with a wrong
multiplier.
- New export test pins the column header and the notes sheet.
- Unit tests pin the Not Assessed rule (`tierFor`), including an all-1s
pillar that must read Traditional. The integration test checks each
pillar's and each system's tier against an answered count computed
separately from the raw rows.
- `make test-unit` and `make test-integration` pass. No OpenAPI drift
and no emberfall changes: emberfall asserts pillar names on
`/scores/aggregate`, not values.

## Deploy notes

- Ship with the matching ztmf-ui PR (same branch name). Its
question-level breakdown uses the same x1.25 factor; if one lands
without the other, question rows and pillar scores disagree.
- On a 9/30 prod copy, every data call drops about 0.4 on average and
roughly half of systems drop one tier; none move up. The comms decision
is tracked on misc#433.
- Outside this repo, the same window: the ztmf-insights reporting PR
plus a `refresh_opdivs.py` run, and the Power BI pillar score measure.
